title: 1990 AHSME Problem 9
statement: Each edge of a cube is colored either red or black. Every face of the cube has at least one black edge. The smallest possible number of black edges is

solutions.text:
Each black edge can cover only its two incident faces, so covering all \(6\) faces requires at least \(3\) black edges. Choose edges incident to the face-pairs top/front, bottom/left, and back/right. These three edges cover all six faces, so the minimum is \(3.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Each edge belongs to exactly two faces
For the matching upper bound, choose three mutually nonadjacent edges
